topic: Procedure Linkage Table (PLT) and Global Offset Table (GOT)
explanation: The Procedure Linkage Table (PLT) and Global Offset Table (GOT) are crucial mechanisms for implementing dynamic linking in position-independent code (PIC).  They allow a program to call functions from shared libraries without knowing their exact memory addresses at compile time.  The PLT acts as an intermediary, resolving function addresses at runtime, while the GOT stores these resolved addresses. This is essential for shared libraries, allowing multiple programs to use the same library code in memory without conflicts.
code_example:
; Global Offset Table (GOT)
; Used for accessing external data or resolved func addresses (PIC)
; %rip is the Instruction Pointer (IP-relative addressing)

    call_label:
        lea     (%rip), %rbx        ; Get current address (Base)
        add     $GOT_OFFSET, %rbx   ; Calculate GOT base address

    ; Read external data 'g_ext_var' address from GOT
        movq    g_ext_var@GOTPCREL(%rbx), %rax
        movl    (%rax), %ecx        ; Load data value

; Procedure Linkage Table (PLT)
; Trampoline used to resolve function addresses at runtime

    external_func@PLT:
        ; 1. Jump via the GOT entry (Indirection)
        jmp     qword ptr [external_func@GOTPCREL]

        ; If first call, GOT points here for dynamic resolution:
        ; 2. Push required relocation index onto stack
        push    $RELOC_INDEX

        ; 3. Jump to the dynamic linker resolver (GOT[2])
        jmp     qword ptr [PLT_RESOLVER_ENTRY]
        ; Linker updates GOT entry; subsequent calls skip steps 2/3
keywords: PLT GOT, Position Independent Code, Procedure Linkage Table, Global Offset Table
